clue.text: Araucaria's £500 crossword?

parts.note: a monkey is British slang for five hundred pounds
a crossword is a puzzle

explanation.surface: A crossword by the late Guardian setter Araucaria, sold for five hundred pounds.
explanation.walkthrough: Araucaria was a famous Guardian setter, so the surface suggests one of his puzzles; but Araucaria is also the Latin genus name of the tree.
explanation.definitionFit: Araucaria is the botanical genus of the monkey puzzle tree, a spiky South American conifer.

clue.text: … beginning to smoke a chillum (new variety)

indicators.note: new tells us the letters are made into a new arrangement
beginning to picks out only the opening letter of smoke

parts.note: taken as written; a chillum is a clay pipe for smoking

explanation.surface: Continuing from the previous clue: someone starts smoking a pipe of a new kind.
explanation.walkthrough: The leading dots tie the surface to 27 across. 'new' rearranges S (the start of 'smoke'), A and CHILLUM.
explanation.definitionFit: Variety is the theatrical entertainment of songs and comic turns that British audiences called music hall.

clue.text: Tweeter is Greek character with thick hair?

parts.note: nu is a letter of the Greek alphabet
a thatch is a thick head of hair

explanation.surface: A singer is a Greek fellow with a bushy mop of hair.
explanation.definitionFit: A tweeter is anything that tweets, here a songbird such as this small tree-climbing species.

clue.text: Deport half of 11 out of 12 shortly

indicators.note: out of here means the first piece stands outside, around the second
half of takes the first three of the six letters

parts.note: eleven written as a word

indicators.note: shortly cuts the last character off the numeral

parts.note: twelve in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: Reads as a cross-reference puzzle: banish part of one answer from another.
explanation.walkthrough: 11 and 12 look like references to other clues (here DECLARE and ELEVENS) but are plain numbers, the second in Roman numerals. 'half of', 'shortly' and 'out of' are the indicators.
explanation.definitionFit: To deport someone is to expel them from a country, which is to send them into exile.

clue.text: Writer was angry, maybe about Thackeray hero

parts.note: a pen is something that writes

indicators.note: about signals that the word is turned round

parts.note: anger is one of the deadly sins, so being angry is one way to have sinned

explanation.surface: An author lost their temper over one of Thackeray's characters.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' reverses SINNED to DENNIS. 'maybe' marks anger as just one example of sinning.
explanation.definitionFit: Arthur Pendennis is the title character of Thackeray's novel The History of Pendennis.

clue.text: Readjusted to show zip (OED)

indicators.note: to show means the letter O is shown spelt out in full as the word it looks like

parts.note: zip is slang for nothing, zero

explanation.surface: A dictionary entry was revised to include the word zip.
explanation.walkthrough: The O of OED looks like a nought, so writing it out as ZERO turns OED into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A gauge or sight that has been readjusted back to its baseline setting has been zeroed.

clue.text: Leftover unpalatable Scotch egg, primarily indicating a bad egg

parts.note: left is L and over is O, the cricket abbreviation

indicators.note: primarily asks for the first letters of the next three words

explanation.surface: A stale leftover Scotch egg (an egg wrapped in sausage meat) is a sign of a bad egg.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Leftover' must be split into 'Left' (L) and 'over' (O, a cricket over).
explanation.definitionFit: A louse is a contemptible person, just as a bad egg is a rotter.

clue.text: Cards passed around

indicators.note: around suggests the letters are moved about into a new order

explanation.surface: Playing cards are handed round the table.
explanation.definitionFit: Spades are one of the four suits in a deck, so a set of such playing cards.

clue.text: Positive indications in last of many letters

indicators.note: last of takes the final letter of many

parts.note: esses are the letters S

explanation.surface: Signs of approval can be found in the final lines of many letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Saying yes is giving agreement, so repeated affirmative answers are positive indications.

clue.text: In a blog entry, one gets put forward

indicators.note: In tells us the numeral goes inside the entry

parts.note: a post is an entry on a blog
one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: Someone proposes an idea in a blog post.
explanation.definitionFit: To posit an idea is to propose or suggest it as a basis for argument.

clue.text: Bike part from Benin? True, surprisingly

indicators.note: surprisingly hints at an unexpected rearrangement of the letters

explanation.surface: Someone is surprised to learn a bicycle component comes from the West African country of Benin.
explanation.definitionFit: A bicycle wheel's tyre contains an inflatable rubber tube, a component of the bike.

clue.text: Whimsically remove 19's county from state

parts.note: the prefix de- means remove, whimsically turning the verb into de-Clare
the clue at 19 mentions Clare, a county in the west of Ireland

explanation.surface: A fanciful plan to cut an Irish county out of a nation.
explanation.walkthrough: To 'de-Clare' something would be to take Clare out of it, a joke on the prefix de-. County Clare is in the Republic of Ireland.
explanation.definitionFit: To state something is to say it formally, to announce or assert it.

clue.text: Teams of 6 making a comeback

indicators.note: making a comeback says the answer's numerals must be read backwards to give the clue's number

parts.note: the answer's meaning written in Roman numerals, XIS, read backwards makes SIX, the number 6

explanation.surface: A clue about a half-dozen of something staging a return.
explanation.walkthrough: A reverse clue: elevens are XIS in Roman numerals, and XIS backwards spells SIX, so the answer is what makes 6 come back.
explanation.definitionFit: A side in football or cricket is an eleven, so several sporting teams are elevens.

clue.text: Unintended eating from tins is back happening? Not at home

indicators.note: is back says the word comes backwards

parts.note: tins are cans

indicators.note: at home is IN, so not at home removes those letters

parts.note: a happening is an incident

explanation.surface: Accidentally eating from tins happens when you're away from home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is back' and 'Not at home' (at home being IN) are the indicators. The answer is a jokey blend of snack and accident, not in most dictionaries.
explanation.definitionFit: A humorous blend of snack and accident, coined for absent-mindedly scoffing food.

clue.text: Fish head removed by daughter during party? That's bold stuff

indicators.note: the fish's first letter is taken away and replaced by the next piece

parts.note: a herring is a fish
a do is a party

explanation.surface: A daughter cuts the head off a fish at a party, a daring act.
explanation.walkthrough: 'head removed by' swaps the H of HERRING for D, giving DERRING.
explanation.definitionFit: Derring-do means heroic courage or daring deeds, so bold action.

clue.text: Flyer billed at length by hotel

definitions.meaning: a bird with a long down-curved bill

explanation.surface: An airline passenger is charged for their stay at a hotel.
explanation.definitionFit: The ibis is a wading bird with a long curved beak, and also the name of a hotel brand.

clue.text: Bottom spot, with blistering pace: ultimately just last on the buzzer

parts.note: bum is slang for bottom
a bleb is a small blister, a spot on the skin

indicators.note: ultimately and last on both ask for final letters, here of pace and of the

explanation.surface: A sporting tale: a team in bottom spot finishing with a burst of speed just before the final hooter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'blistering' hints at BLEB, a blister; 'just' is padding the parse leaves aside.
explanation.definitionFit: The bumblebee is the large furry bee known for its loud buzzing.

clue.text: Pair of coppers employed for a trivial sum

parts.note: a pair is two
British pennies are copper coins, pence

explanation.surface: Two police officers are hired for very little money.
explanation.walkthrough: 'coppers' suggests police but means copper coins.
explanation.definitionFit: Twopence is a tiny amount of money, used to mean something worth almost nothing.

clue.text: Rook? It's a bird

definitions.meaning: to rook someone is to cheat or swindle them

explanation.surface: Is a rook a bird? Yes, it is.
explanation.definitionFit: To gull someone is to dupe them, the same as rooking them; a gull is also a seabird.

clue.text: Manages to understand both Sun and Times

parts.note: to get something is to understand it
S is the abbreviation for Sunday
by means times in multiplication, as in three by four

explanation.surface: Someone copes well enough to follow both the Sun and the Times newspapers.
explanation.walkthrough: The Sun and the Times are British daily newspapers.
explanation.definitionFit: To get by is to cope or survive on limited resources.

clue.text: Who am I, off with sister on vacation in Clare, perhaps?

indicators.note: off suggests the letters are disordered
on vacation means emptied, leaving only the outer letters

explanation.surface: Someone abroad in County Clare with their sister asks who they are.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on vacation' empties 'sister' to SR; 'off' rearranges WHOAMI with SR and IN. Clare is also a woman's name.
explanation.definitionFit: Clare is a woman's name, so a woman called Clare from Ireland would be one.

clue.text: Maybe 19's fate, after swallowing two tablets

indicators.note: swallowing means taking in, so the first piece goes round the second

parts.note: the Norns were the Fates of Norse mythology
E stands for an ecstasy tablet, so two of them are two Es

explanation.surface: An Irish woman's destiny after taking two pills.
explanation.definitionFit: Noreen is a girl's name of Irish origin, so an example of an Irishwoman's name.

clue.text: Bloomer occurring more regularly, we hear

indicators.note: we hear tells us the answer only matches the spoken word

parts.note: occurring more regularly could be daily-er, dailier

explanation.surface: A blunder that keeps happening more often.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bloomer' looks like a mistake but means a flower.
explanation.definitionFit: A dahlia is a garden plant grown for its showy flowers, so something that blooms.

clue.text: Am I nuts swimming in this? Yes

definitions.text: Am I nuts swimming in this? Yes

indicators.note: swimming suggests the letters are moving around

explanation.surface: Someone wonders if they are mad to swim in a giant wave; the answer is yes.
explanation.definitionFit: A tsunami is a huge sea wave, and only a madman would swim in one.

clue.text: Ineligible female included in squad

indicators.note: included in says the letter goes inside the group

parts.note: a squad is a unit

explanation.surface: A woman in a team turns out not to qualify.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone unfit for a role does not meet its requirements, so is not qualified.

clue.text: Suffering ups and downs, as extremely nervous?

definitions.meaning: having the mood swings of ... disorder
the extremes of nervous are N and S, the two poles, so having both poles

explanation.surface: Someone with mood swings is also very anxious.
explanation.walkthrough: The ends of NERVOUS are N and S, North and South: two poles, bi-polar.
explanation.definitionFit: Bipolar disorder causes swings between high and low moods; and two poles is bi-polar.

clue.text: Sort of jazz dance covered by black European

indicators.note: in a down entry, covered by means the dance comes below the other pieces

parts.note: B is the abbreviation for black, as on pencils
to bop is to dance

explanation.surface: A dancer from Europe in black clothes.
explanation.definitionFit: Bebop is the fast, complex style of jazz developed in the 1940s by Charlie Parker and others.

clue.text: Long-winded government-speak? Floundering fleabag fibs regularly

indicators.note: floundering means struggling clumsily, so the letters are thrown into disorder
regularly takes every other letter of fibs

explanation.surface: A shabby person keeps telling lies while struggling to explain themselves.
explanation.walkthrough: 'regularly' takes F and B from FIBS; 'Floundering' rearranges them with FLEABAG.
explanation.definitionFit: Bafflegab is wordy, confusing jargon, the sort of thing officials say.

clue.text: Le Bon compilation? Great!

indicators.note: a compilation puts things together in a new order, here the letters

explanation.surface: A greatest hits album by Duran Duran singer Simon Le Bon would be wonderful.
explanation.definitionFit: Noble means great in character or rank, magnificent.

clue.text: Eight Miles High? One's in this guitar shop, playing before …

definitions.text: Eight Miles High? One's in this

parts.note: the Strat is the Fender Stratocaster electric guitar

indicators.note: playing suggests the letters are played about with

parts.note: ere is an old word for before

explanation.surface: Someone plays the Byrds song Eight Miles High in a guitar shop.
explanation.walkthrough: 'playing' rearranges SHOP to OSPH. The dots lead into 1 down.
explanation.definitionFit: The stratosphere begins roughly six to ten miles up, so an aircraft at eight miles is in it.
